note: Wren Phonics — Year 2 spelling progression outline, for the whole year. Statutory rules and the full common-exception word list are transcribed from NC English Appendix 1 (DfE, 2013), "Spelling - work for year 2", verified against the gov.uk PDF 2026-10-08. Explanatory wording is Wren's own paraphrase. provenance: Wren original, b410, 2026-10-08.
lesson_structure: Same four-part shape as the core phonics routine, renamed for spelling: Warm up -> Teach the pattern -> Have a go -> Use it.

rules.title: The /dʒ/ sound spelt ge and dge at the end of words, and sometimes g before e, i, y
rules.guidance: The letter "j" is never used for this sound at the end of an English word. Straight after a short vowel sound, it is spelt -dge; after any other sound it is spelt -ge. Inside a word, this sound is often (not always) spelt g before e, i or y.

rules.title: The /s/ sound spelt c before e, i, y
rules.guidance: A "c" says /s/ specifically when it comes before e, i or y.

rules.title: The /n/ sound spelt kn and (less often) gn at the beginning of words
rules.guidance: The "k" and "g" were pronounced hundreds of years ago and are now silent.

rules.title: The /r/ sound spelt wr at the beginning of words
rules.guidance: Also reflects an old pronunciation — the "w" is silent.

rules.title: The /l/ or /əl/ sound spelt -le at the end of words
rules.guidance: The most common spelling for this ending.

rules.title: The /l/ or /əl/ sound spelt -el at the end of words
rules.guidance: Less common than -le; often follows m, n, r, s, v or w.

rules.title: The /l/ or /əl/ sound spelt -al at the end of words
rules.guidance: Not many nouns end this way, but many adjectives do.

rules.title: Words ending -il
rules.guidance: A small, learn-them group.

rules.title: The /aɪ/ sound spelt -y at the end of words
rules.guidance: By far the most common spelling for this sound at the end of a word.

rules.title: Adding -es to nouns and verbs ending in -y
rules.guidance: The y changes to i before -es is added.

rules.title: Adding -ed, -ing, -er and -est to a root word ending in -y with a consonant before it
rules.guidance: The y changes to i before -ed, -er, -est — but NOT before -ing (that would make "ii").

rules.title: Adding -ing, -ed, -er, -est and -y to words ending in -e with a consonant before it
rules.guidance: Drop the final -e before adding an ending that starts with a vowel letter. Exception: "being".

rules.title: Adding -ing, -ed, -er, -est and -y to one-syllable words ending in a single consonant after a single vowel (doubling)
rules.guidance: Double the last consonant to keep the vowel sound short. Exception: "x" is never doubled.

rules.title: The /ɔː/ sound spelt a before l and ll
rules.guidance: Usually spelt "a" before l/ll, not the more common "or".

rules.title: The /ʌ/ sound spelt o
rules.guidance: There are only a few of these words — learn which words use this spelling.

rules.title: The /iː/ sound spelt -ey
rules.guidance: The plural of these words just adds -s.

rules.title: The /ɒ/ sound spelt a after w and qu
rules.guidance: "a" is the most common spelling for this sound after w/qu.

rules.title: The /ɜː/ sound spelt or after w
rules.guidance: There are only a few of these words — learn which words use this spelling.

rules.title: The /ɔː/ sound spelt ar after w
rules.guidance: There are only a few of these words — learn which words use this spelling.

rules.title: The /ʒ/ sound spelt s
rules.guidance: There are only a few of these words — learn which words use this spelling.

rules.title: The suffixes -ment, -ness, -ful, -less and -ly
rules.guidance: Added straight onto most root words with no spelling change. Exceptions: "argument", and a -y root word with a consonant before it (more than one syllable) changes y to i.

rules.title: Contractions
rules.guidance: The apostrophe marks where a letter (or letters) would be if the words were written in full. "It’s" means "it is" or "it has" — never the possessive.

rules.title: The possessive apostrophe (singular nouns)
rules.guidance: Add 's to a singular noun to show it owns something.

rules.title: Words ending in -tion
rules.guidance: A very common word-ending pattern.

rules.title: Homophones and near-homophones
rules.guidance: Words that sound the same (or nearly) but mean different things and are spelt differently — the meaning has to come from context.
